title: 03 Functions: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Lines Become Functions | six relations - the line y = 2x + 1 from lesson 02, y = |x|, a circle, x = y², the vertical line x = 3 and a table with a repeated x - swept by a draggable vertical line that counts the outputs at that input | a relation is a function exactly when every input has one output, which is what the vertical line test measures; repeated outputs are free, repeated inputs with different outputs are fatal

2. The Function Machine | f(x) = 2x + 1, x² − 4 and 1/(x − 2) evaluated live at a draggable input a and shift h, with f(a + h), f(a) + h, f(a)·h, f(−a), −f(a) and the x-left-unchanged error all computed side by side | f(x) is an instruction to substitute the input for every x, so f(a + h) is one evaluation at a + h and each distractor is a correct computation of something that was not asked

3. Domain And Range | two number lines, one shaded where the input is allowed and one shaded where the output is reachable, with a draggable candidate x and candidate y tested against 1/(x − 3), √(x − 2), x² and 2x + 1 | the domain is the possible inputs and the range the possible outputs; only zero denominators and negative even radicands exclude anything, and boundary values like x = 2 and y = 0 are included

4. Sign Versus Direction | a curve chosen from x² − 4, x² − 9, x³, −x² + 4x and −x² + 6x with the negative stretch banded on the axis, a draggable point showing f(x) and f'(x) as two separate verdicts, and the intervals recomputed by sampling | sign says above or below the axis and direction says climbing or falling, and they are independent - x³ is increasing everywhere while negative on the whole left half - with each end of a negative stretch an x-intercept

5. The Inverse Mirror | f(x) = 3x − 1, x³ and x² drawn with their reflections across the dashed line y = x, a draggable point sending (a, b) to (b, a), and a horizontal test line that counts how many times it cuts the graph | forming the inverse interchanges inputs and outputs, which reflects the graph across y = x, and the inverse is a function only when the original is one-to-one, which the horizontal line test decides
